blogTitle: ALL ABOARD: The Official Add Train Blog (Now Boarding)
about: HI!!! I'm Adam and I have 10,412 friends!!! (that's as of 3:41 this morning!!! it changes!!!) I run the Add Train. You add the person above you, you add the person below you, you comment 'choo choo' on both, and everybody ends up with MORE friends!!! It's the greatest idea I ever had and I've had it 214 times. I say 'thanks 4 the add' to every single person who adds me and honestly sometimes to people who didn't (I get excited). I do pc4pc, c4c and t4t (top 8 trades, ask me). If you're my friend, you're my friend forever. Even the ones I haven't met yet!!! (all of you) (so far). ALL ABOARD!!!
aboutMore: Fun stats!!! Friends: 10,412. Friends I've met in person: 0. (0 is a start!!!) Birthdays I know: 3,211. Messages sent today: 61. Replies: 4. I'm not worried about the ratio, a reply is a reply!!! I work the drive-thru window at the Dairy Dream so I'm on here between 2 and 4 AM when it's quiet and everybody's green dot is on. Mom says go to bed. Mom is right. Mom is always right.

(all of you!!!) but also todd, the guy who started this, so I can say thank you for the add (he was my friend #1 and I still think about it). my 10,000th friend, a guy named Kevin R. who wrote back 'k.' (I saved it). and whoever's reading this at 3 AM right now and thinking 'same.' (hi. same.)

blog.title: 10,000 FRIENDS!!!! (A Message To All 10,000 Of You)
blog.body: IT HAPPENED!!! At 12:14 AM I got friend request #10,000 and I screamed (quietly, my mom was asleep). It was from a guy named Kevin R. who wrote 'k.' I saved it in a folder. I want to thank everybody who ever added me, commented, joined a train, or said 'choo choo' back. My mom made a cake. It said 10,000 in blue. We ate it in the kitchen, just us, and it was a really good cake. She cut two slices and said 'one for you and one for you,' which is a joke we have. Afterward I made a list of thank-yous. 10,000 names. It took four hours. When I got to the end I noticed I don't know a single thing about most of you except your default picture. I'd like to. So here's the deal: tell me one thing about you. Anything. I'll write it next to your name in the spreadsheet. Choo choo.

blog.title: THE ADD TRAIN TURNS ONE: 214 TRAINS, 6 THINGS I LEARNED
blog.body: One year, 214 trains!!! Here's what I learned. 1) 9 PM is the best time to leave the station. 2) 'choo choo' gets 1 reply in 20. 'hi' gets 1 in 60. Trains are friendlier. 3) Some people add you and never say a word. That's okay. It's like a nod from across a party. 4) The Late Train (2 AM) derailed this week. 3 people said 'stop adding me,' 1 said 'who is this,' 1 said 'lol.' I'm counting the 'lol' as a win. Laughing is a feeling. 5) My mom asked how many of my friends I've met and I said 'it's not about meeting, Mom, it's about the number,' and she said 'okay, sweetheart,' and didn't look at me. 6) The kitchen is quiet at 3 AM. The router blinks. I like the blink. All aboard. - Adam

blog.title: A LIST OF EVERYONE WHO WROTE BACK THIS MONTH (THANK YOU!!!)
blog.body: Thank-yous!!! People who wrote back to me in September: Mr. Henderson (twice, one was a style guide), Kyle (4 times, all 'hi,' all perfect), Debbie (a Dell, I think about it daily), Mr. Whiskers (a cat) (he said 'acknowledged'), Walt (a LETTER, on paper, well, sort of, it said 'Dear Adam' at the top), and my mom (in person, with a cake, for my 18th birthday on the 6th). That's 41 replies out of 1,900 messages. I made a chart: 2.1 percent!!! That's a really good rate if you think about it. Some people's mail is 100 percent bills. My favorite reply was Walt's, because he asked how many of you I've sat down to supper with, and I counted, and I was gonna say a number, but then I just said 'my mom.' He said that's a good number to start with. Choo choo.
